title: Repeated Substring Pattern
statement: Return true when `s` can be built by concatenating a nonempty substring with itself at least twice.
hints: If s is made of a repeated block, then s appears in (s + s) before the last character and after the first.
The KMP prefix table gives the same fact: if n % (n - lps[n - 1]) == 0 and lps[n - 1] is nonzero, the string repeats.

approaches.name: Try every divisor
approaches.explanation: A period must divide the length.

editorial: Let t = s + s. If s is periodic, a second copy starts at the period inside t, so s is found strictly inside t, not only at the two ends. Conversely, a match inside t[1:-1] means a rotation of s equals s, which is exactly a repeated block. haystack.find on the sliced concatenation is the short proof. The KMP border is the interview follow-up.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def repeated_substring_pattern(s: str) -> bool:
    return s in (s + s)[1:-1]
